card.title: Report Writing and Summarisation — news & event report format

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **What it is:** factual, third-person, past-tense reporting of an event (sports day, blood donation camp) — not a story, not an opinion.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Trick 1: Report skeleton: title, byline, intro (what/when/where), body (details in past tense, third person), conclusion (outcome/recommendation) — the five blocks are the marks.
Trick 2: Reports are OBJECTIVE: no 'I think', no exaggeration; add one quotation or number for credibility.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Summarisation partner skill:** compress any passage into its core idea in your own words within the word limit — keep the author's viewpoint, drop examples and repetition.  ·  **Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Write a report on a school science exhibition in about 120 words. (4 marks) — title, byline, 5W intro, two body details, closing outcome.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ```svg Report funnel: many facts, one recommendation <svg viewBox="0 0 640 200" font-family="Segoe UI" font-size="13"><rect x="0" y="0" width="640" height="200" fill="#ffffff"/><g text-anchor="middle"><path d="M140 60 L 500 60 L 380 130 L 260 130 Z" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#1d4ed8"/><text x="320" y="95" fill="#1d4ed8" font-size="12">findings</text><rect x="270" y="140" width="100" height="34" rx="8" fill="#f0fdf4"…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Structure:** Headline (short, factual) → Byline ('By a Staff Reporter') + dateline ('Kathmandu, 12 May:') → Lead paragraph answering WHO did WHAT, WHERE, WHEN, WHY in 2–3 sentences → Body in chronological order → a short quotation from the chief guest → closing outcome.  ·  **Tense/voice grammar:** past simple for every event; passive voice is standard for ceremony facts ('trophies were distributed'); reported speech for quotes; third person only — never 'I'.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 3: Summary method: read twice → one line per paragraph → join with connectors → compress to 1/3 length in your own words; never copy sentences.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. How long should a summary be? (1 mark) — about one-third of the original, in your own words.

rows.text: **Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).
